title: Committed app.bin: 2MB compiled binary added by the PR (chunk adds it as mode 100755)
evidence:
chunk-6 diff: "diff --git a/app.bin b/app.bin
new file mode 100755
index 0000000..4aaf130
Binary files /dev/null and b/app.bin differ"; git ls-files -s app.bin → "100755 4aaf130a4825b3b67a49e713b76ee83b9e244843 0	app.bin"; .gitignore in this chunk adds only "tools/raylib-sw/", "bin/", "goldens/_reports/" — app.bin is not excluded
detail: Round briefing: "The committed app.bin (2MB binary) — the 0118cc0 commit added a built binary to the repo. Build artifacts should not be committed (bloats the repo, platform-specific)." Platform-specific executable, unprotected by .gitignore.
recommended_fix: git rm --cached app.bin and add "app.bin" to .gitignore; README already documents `odin build app` as the build path.

title: Committed self-review docs describe a pre-fix codebase — their headline blockers are false against the reviewed commit
evidence: Doc B1: "Mis-sized or corrupt golden silently PASSES the T2 pixel compare ... check_golden fails only `if mismatch > 0`" vs harness/goldens.odin: "if mismatch < 0 { ... append(fails, fmt.tprintf(\"T2 %dms: golden corrupt or wrong size — cannot compare (re-bless deliberately)\", ms)) } else if mismatch > 0 {". Doc W10: "`harness replay` passes vacuously: prefix-only compare" vs harness/replay.odin: "replayed, ok := replay_hashes(log_path, catalogs, u64(man.ticks), false, &fails)" and measured output "harness replay: 3000 ticks verified against the manifest — bit-for-bit (ODN-11)". Doc: "error404: manifest-matched through **121 of 250** ticks" vs measured "250 ticks verified against the manifest". Doc: "Balance knobs that do nothing: `rolling_window_ticks`" vs core/flow.odin:87 "f.roll_window = cat.balance.rolling_window_ticks" + core/catalog.odin:388 "if b.rolling_window_ticks <= 0 || b.rolling_window_ticks > ROLLING_MAX {". Doc: "crises.json ... never parsed" vs core/catalog.odin:317 "v, e := json.parse(src.crises, parse_integers = true)". Doc: "the upgrade command is reachable only from core unit tests" vs harness/demo_parse.odin:136 "case \"upgrade_pipe\":" + demos/draw_and_upgrade.dem (harness run PASS)
detail: Both docs claim open blockers/warnings (T2 silent pass, replay prefix-only, no QoS gap-fill, E30 absent, no E17 barrier, no bare fixture, batch budget bugs, upgrade unreachable) that the final commit already fixes; readers of the repo's own review trail see phantom blockers.
recommended_fix: Mark each fixed finding in the committed docs (e.g. "FIXED at 0118cc0") or re-run the two reviews against the final commit before merging.

title: Bootstrap and testkit discard lookup `ok` — renamed catalog ids silently map to index 0 (§7.1 no-dropped-returns)
evidence: core/run.odin:56-58: "host, _ := node_type_index(cat, \"content_host\")", "res, _ := node_type_index(cat, \"residential\")", "mid, _ := node_type_index(cat, \"router_mid\")"; core/testkit.odin:16: "wide, _ := tier_index(cat, \"wide\")", :61 "streaming, _ := class_index(cat, \"streaming\")", :75-76 "wide, _ := tier_index(cat, \"wide\")", "standard, _ := tier_index(cat, \"standard\")"; tools/lint.sh gate 4: "HITS=$(grep -rnE '^\s*_ = ' core/*.odin | grep -v '_test\.odin' || true)"
detail: A node_types.json/pipe_tiers.json rename returns (0, false) and the discard keeps 0 — the boot map silently builds with the wrong type/tier and the sim misbehaves with zero error. Lint gate 4 misses multi-assign discards.
recommended_fix: Check each `ok` and raise the fail-fast catalog error; extend lint gate 4 to also match ', _ :=' discards of fallible lookups.

title: E1 severance pin cannot fail: the shipped test never puts a packet on the pipe it demolishes
evidence: Test body: "// run traffic until the direct leg is in use, then demolish it" ... "for tick in u64(1) ..= 20 { flow_step(state, tick, &plan) }" ... "dem := Command{kind = Cmd_Demolish{target = direct.pipe, is_node = false}}" ... "if delivered_after <= delivered_before { tfail(t, \"reroute must keep deliveries flowing\") }"; all drawn legs are "tier = wide" (40 u/s); the severed-pipe pass (core/flow.odin:485-496) fires only when "_, ok := pipe_slot(t, p.route[p.edge_idx]); ok" fails — uncongested wide pipes let every packet complete its edge within the tick it enters (progress_units += served), so none is in flight at demolish; no occupancy or Ev_Packet_Dropped{.Severance} assertion exists
detail: The test named as closing Perkins r1 "Demolish-in-transit reroute/severance untested" passes via new spawns re-routing around the removed leg; deleting the severed-pipe pass would leave all 30 tests + 7 goldens green. E1 is pinned by a test that cannot fail.
recommended_fix: Congest the direct leg first (flood pattern from test_qos_priority_protects_its_class), assert non-zero occupancy on the leg, then assert reroute or a Severance drop event.

title: crises.json is parsed and hashed but its fields are never consumed — editing it forces a re-bless with zero behavior change
evidence: core/catalog.odin:317-322: "v, e := json.parse(src.crises, parse_integers = true)", "if e != nil { return cat, {\"crises.json\", \"$\", \"invalid JSON\"} }", "if !oke { return cat, {\"crises.json\", \"entries\", \"missing array\"} }"; core/catalog.odin:153: "mix(&h, src.crises)"; grep for Crisis_Def/preventive_redesign/lead_time_ticks across core/, app/, harness/ → zero uses outside catalog.odin; data/crises.json ships "\"preventive_redesign\": \"Add capacity/redundancy on the content-host legs...\"" and "\"lead_time_ticks\": 600"
detail: The catalog's crises block validates and hashes into catalog_hash but no code reads the archetype metadata; tuning crises.json triggers the T1 "catalog drift" gate and a mandatory re-bless while changing nothing — drift bait, and a recurrence of the Perkins #20 loaded-never-applied class.
recommended_fix: Wire preventive_redesign/lead_time_ticks into the HUD/forecast path or drop the unused fields from the shipped catalog.

title: core/run.odin header comment contradicts the step body on the E23 batch path
detail: The pinned step-order comment names topology_apply_all as phase 1, but step applies log entries individually via topology_apply_edit; topology_apply_all's only callers are tests (topology_test.odin:222-268). The header misleads any future editor of the batch path.
recommended_fix: Reword the header comment to "apply logged commands individually (not as one E23 batch — see body)".
